The sentencing process
A Scottish Sentencing Council consultation
Page 7 of 31
Developing sentencing guidelines
A key part of our role in promoting consistency is to prepare sentencing guidelines for the
Scottish courts. These guidelines must be approved by the High Court of Justiciary before
they have any effect. When sentencing an offender, a court4 must have regard to any
relevant sentencing guidelines in relation to the case. If a court decides not to follow the
guidelines, the judge must state the reasons for that decision.
Sentencing guidelines can be general and cover all offences. Or they can be more specific
and cover a particular offence or group of offences.
As a first step, we have decided to prepare a set of three general guidelines. We held a
public consultation on our first guideline, ‘Principles and purposes of sentencing’, in summer
